title: Recommendation for a fully automated AI trading bot available in the UAE
author: Upper_Tennis8847
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I’m based in the UAE, and I’m looking for recommendations for a fully automated AI trading system.   
What I want is simple: I deposit my money, and the system does everything else.

Any recommendation? 

Thanks

comments.author: TheKillerScope
comments.body:
First of all, be very careful what bots you connect your wallet to or what platform you send money to. Unless it is a reputable website or platform, stay away!!!

There have been plenty of victims who deposited money into a sketchy platform, then were roped into depositing more because they make more profit, and when the time actually came to take the money out... well... good luck.

replies.author: Upper_Tennis8847
replies.body: I understand exactly what you mean, this is why I am looking for some recommendation to test it out. Thanks

replies.author: TheKillerScope
replies.body: Whomever DM's you a platform has no good intentions. Good luck!

replies.author: SnooBooks638
replies.body: I’m working on an open-source trading infrastructure but it doesn’t trade or create strategies for you out of the box. You create the strategies and it helps you optimize them by making suggestions and identifying the gaps in the system. The execution is deterministic based on the rules and the strategies you set. It’s available at https://github.com/toniton/ml-crypto-trading. But you have to put in the work (riotrading.app is where you can see it in play)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: nothing legit works as deposit and walk away, and the ones advertising it are where most of these stories end badly. any real bot needs someone choosing the rule and watching it, and a few months on paper before any money goes near it.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I can't recommend one, because "deposit and the system does everything" is also the exact pitch used by most investment scams, so the first step is verifying the company, not the bot. Check that the firm is licensed with a UAE regulator that covers its activity (the Securities and Commodities Authority, DFSA or ADGM's FSRA for securities, VARA for virtual assets in Dubai) by looking it up on the regulator's own register, and avoid anything that promises fixed returns or asks you to send funds to a personal or crypto wallet. Ask for a verified live record of at least a year with fees and drawdown, and whether you keep custody in your own brokerage account. Before depositing real money, run any strategy on paper for a few weeks and compare it with simply holding an index fund. Backtest Labs at Cymetica is one place to see how strategy results are compared against a benchmark.
